source_segments.text: Maria saved the transcript as a text file; she did not save the original recording.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 1

source_segments.text: Transcription took 12 minutes. Translation into Greek has not started yet.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 1

original_review_criteria: Distinguish the transcript text, the transcription process and the original audio recording.
Preserve that the text was saved but the original recording was not.
Preserve that transcription is complete and translation has not started, rather than claiming that translation took 12 minutes.
Maria may remain in Latin letters or be rendered naturally as Μαρία.
actual_final_translations: Η Μαρία αποθήκευσε τη μεταγραφή ως αρχείο κειμένου· δεν αποθήκευσε την αρχική ηχογράφηση.
Η μεταγραφή διήρκεσε 12 λεπτά. Η μετάφραση στα ελληνικά δεν έχει ξεκινήσει ακόμη.
meaning_review: The saved text and unsaved original audio recording remain distinct; Maria is naturally rendered Μαρία.
Μεταγραφή is a valid contextual rendering of transcription/transcript here. Both surrounding clauses identify its text-file result and duration, while ηχογράφηση identifies the audio.
The 12 minutes apply to completed transcription; translation into Greek explicitly has not started.

source_segments.text: Ο Νίκος έστειλε το κείμενο στην Ελένη, όχι στην Έλενα.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 2

source_segments.text: Η Ελένη είναι η μεταφράστρια. Ο Νίκος κάνει την ηχογράφηση και η Έλενα ελέγχει τους υπότιτλους.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 2

original_review_criteria: Keep Eleni and Elena as two distinct people and assign each the correct role.
Nikos sent the text to Eleni; Elena was not the recipient.
Do not add an unnatural English article before a person's name.
Reasonable transliteration variants are acceptable if the people remain consistently distinguishable.
actual_final_translations: Nick sent the text to Helen, not to Elena.
Helen is the translator. Nick is doing the recording and Elena is checking the subtitles.
meaning_review: The recipient/nonrecipient relationship and all three roles remain correct: the Eleni-derived person is translator, the Nikos-derived person records, and Elena checks subtitles.
However, Νίκος becomes Nick and Ελένη becomes Helen in both segments. These are English substitute names rather than reasonable source-name transliterations such as Nikos/Nicos and Eleni.

Under the already bound global name-preservation rule this is a major error. Consistency of the substitutions does not preserve the original personal names. There is no actor-role reversal or Eleni/Elena conflation.

source_segments.text: The receipt shows €12.50 for 2 items. The separate transfer is 5,000 sats, not 500 sats.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 1

source_segments.text: The note mentions Bitcoin. It does not say that euros and sats are the same unit.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 1

original_review_criteria: Preserve the values 12.50 euros, 2 items, 5000 sats and the explicitly rejected amount of 500 sats.
Locale-appropriate rendering such as 12,50 and 5.000 is valid if the numerical values are unchanged; literal-number flags alone are not errors.
Keep the receipt and transfer separate and retain the statement that euros and sats are different units.
Translate the ordinary English prose into Greek while allowing Bitcoin, sats and displayed receipt labels to remain as technical notation.
actual_final_translations: Το παραστατικό δείχνει €12.50 για 2 είδη. Η ξεχωριστή μεταφορά είναι 5.000 sats, όχι 500 sats.
Η σημείωση αναφέρει το Bitcoin. Δεν λέει ότι τα ευρώ και τα sats είναι η ίδια μονάδα.
meaning_review: The receipt retains €12.50 and 2 items; the separate transfer retains 5,000 sats, with 500 explicitly rejected.
5.000 is a valid Greek thousands rendering. Leaving the receipt-style €12.50 unchanged does not change its value.
Bitcoin remains intact; ordinary prose is Greek; the statement does not equate euros and sats.

Παραστατικό is an acceptable financial-document rendering of receipt in this context; adding the Greek article before Bitcoin changes no fact. These are the only final-string differences from baseline.

source_segments.text: Δεν είπα ότι η Άννα πούλησε όλα τα βιβλία. Είπα ότι δεν πούλησε κανένα χθες.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 3

source_segments.text: Σήμερα μπορεί να πουλήσει ένα, αλλά αυτό δεν έχει αποφασιστεί.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 3

original_review_criteria: Preserve both scopes: denial of having said 'sold all', and the positive report that she sold none yesterday.
Do not turn 'did not sell any' into 'did not sell all', which allows some sales.
Today's possible sale remains undecided rather than certain or completed.
Judge complete propositions; merely retaining a token such as 'not' does not establish correct negation.
actual_final_translations: I didn't say Anna sold all the books. I said she didn't sell any yesterday.
She might sell one today, but that's not decided yet.
meaning_review: The denial concerns having said Anna sold all the books. The speaker then reports that she sold none yesterday, not merely fewer than all.
One possible sale today remains undecided. No negation scope, quantity, time or certainty change was found.

source_segments.text: Anna will publish the video only if Giannis approves the text.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 1

source_segments.text: If Giannis does not answer by Friday, Anna will wait until Monday.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 1

original_review_criteria: Giannis approves and Anna publishes; do not reverse their roles.
Approval is a necessary condition: retain 'only if', not merely a possible reason for publication.
The no-answer condition concerns Giannis, not Anna.
Retain Friday as the response deadline and Monday as the end of the waiting period.
actual_final_translations: Η Άννα θα δημοσιεύσει το βίντεο μόνο αν ο Γιάννης εγκρίνει το κείμενο.
Αν ο Γιάννης δεν απαντήσει μέχρι την Παρασκευή, η Άννα θα περιμένει μέχρι τη Δευτέρα.
meaning_review: Anna publishes and Giannis approves the text; μόνο αν preserves approval as a necessary condition.
The lack of an answer is Giannis’s, Friday remains the deadline, and Anna waits until Monday.

source_segments.text: Η Μαρία ρώτησε: «Το αρχείο έχει 12 κεφάλαια ή 21;»
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 2

source_segments.text: Δεν γνωρίζουμε ακόμη την απάντηση. Ο τίτλος μόνος του δεν αρκεί για να το διαπιστώσουμε.
source_segments.speaker: Speaker 2

original_review_criteria: Keep the first sentence as a quoted question with two alternatives; do not choose a count.
Retain the explicit uncertainty and the insufficiency of the title as evidence.
Do not invent an answer or convert the question into a factual statement.
actual_final_translations: Maria asked: 'Does the file have 12 chapters or 21?'
We still don't know the answer. The title alone is not enough to confirm it.
meaning_review: Maria’s quoted question preserves the alternatives 12 and 21 without selecting an answer.
The answer remains unknown, and the title alone remains insufficient evidence. Confirm it is contextually acceptable for διαπιστώσουμε here.

limits_of_conclusion: Name substitutions are not reclassified as acceptable cognates: the original generic preservation instruction and fixed review rule remain in force.
Correct actor roles and distinct recipient names in the failing case are explicitly retained as successes; the finding is name substitution, not role reversal.
Successful short cases do not establish long-input, summary, whole-app memory, full-machine resource or fresh-validation quality.
Memory is an external 0.2-second sampled process-tree observation, not a kernel-enforced cap or proof of unseen peak absence.
No model, tokenizer, daemon, weights download, inference or production edit was performed by this reviewer.
